If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue arises in the StringUtils.join(Object[] array, String separator) method, which internally calls the StringUtils.join(Object[] array, String separator, int startIndex, int endIndex) method. The relevant code snippet from the detailed join method shows that it does not defensively handle the case where array elements' toString() method returns null.

Specifically, in the join method:
- The StringBuilder buffer is initialized using the length of the string representation of the first element in the range `(array[startIndex].toString().length())`. If array[startIndex].toString() returns null, this will cause a NullPointerException, as the code attempts to call `length()` on null.
- In the for loop, it appends `array[i]` directly to the StringBuilder, relying on the `StringBuilder.append(Object)` method which internally calls `String.valueOf(Object)`. This method is null-safe in the sense that if `toString()` returns null, it converts it to "null". So, this part is safe.
- The error is thus at the initialization of the StringBuilder capacity, where toString() is called without null checking.

The current bug report's example demonstrates the problem: an object whose overridden toString() returns null will cause the join method to throw NullPointerException because of this unchecked call.

The test case fails as it expects that the join method will gracefully handle null-string values in the array and produce a joined string, but instead receives an NPE.

Recent bug reports do not provide relevant information relating to this null-toString issue.

In summary, the root cause is missing null-check handling on array elements' toString() results when the StringBuilder buffer size is being pre-allocated in join, leading to NPE when toString returns null.

This diagnosis fully explains the failure in testJoin_Objectarray and the nature of the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
